title: Completion of a local ring with finite-dimensional special fibre is finite over the completion of the base
statement: Let $\varphi:(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local homomorphism of local rings ($\varphi(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$) such that the ideals $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak n$ are finitely generated and $S/\mathfrak mS$ is a finite-dimensional vector space over $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, where $\mathfrak m^kS$ denotes the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m^k)$. Let $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_kR/\mathfrak m^k$ and $S^\wedge=\varprojlim_kS/\mathfrak n^k$ be the $\mathfrak m$-adic and $\mathfrak n$-adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\varphi^\wedge:R^\wedge\to S^\wedge$ the ring map $(r_k\bmod\mathfrak m^k)_k\mapsto(\varphi(r_k)\bmod\mathfrak n^k)_k$ (well defined since $\varphi(\mathfrak m^k)\subseteq\mathfrak n^k$). Let $S'=\varprojlim_kS/\mathfrak m^kS$ be the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $S$; since $\mathfrak m^kS\subseteq\mathfrak n^k$ the quotient maps $S/\mathfrak m^kS\to S/\mathfrak n^k$ induce a ring map $\gamma:S'\to S^\wedge$. Then (1) $\gamma$ is an isomorphism, i.e. $S^\wedge$ is the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $S$; and (2) $S^\wedge$, an $R^\wedge$-module via $\varphi^\wedge$, is a finitely generated $R^\wedge$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0394 (lemma-finite-after-completion, line 23100); its proof uses Lemmas 0319 (lemma-change-ideal-completion), 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated) and 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring)

proof.text: Since $\varphi$ is local, $\mathfrak mS\subseteq\mathfrak n\ne S$, so $S/\mathfrak mS$ is a nonzero commutative ring, a $\kappa$-algebra via $R/\mathfrak m\to S/\mathfrak mS$ induced by $\varphi$, of finite dimension over $\kappa$ by hypothesis; by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian] it is an Artinian ring. Its maximal ideals are $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak mS$ for the maximal ideals $\mathfrak q\supseteq\mathfrak mS$ of $S$, and $\mathfrak n$ is the only maximal ideal of $S$; so $S/\mathfrak mS$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak mS$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime] every prime ideal of $S/\mathfrak mS$ equals $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak mS$; since the primes of $S/\mathfrak mS$ are the $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak mS$ with $\mathfrak p\supseteq\mathfrak mS$ prime in $S$, $\mathfrak n$ is the only prime ideal of $S$ containing $\mathfrak mS$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0394 (lemma-finite-after-completion, line 23100), proof: 'mR\subset n because R -> S is local ... S/mS is an Artinian ring, see Lemma 00J6. Hence has dimension 0, see Lemma 00KH'

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], $\sqrt{\mathfrak mS}$ is the intersection of the primes of $S$ containing $\mathfrak mS$, which by Step 1 is $\mathfrak n$: $\mathfrak n=\sqrt{\mathfrak mS}$. As $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated and $\mathfrak n\subseteq\sqrt{\mathfrak mS}$, [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] gives $t\ge1$ with $\mathfrak n^t\subseteq\mathfrak mS$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0394 (lemma-finite-after-completion, line 23100), proof: 'hence n = sqrt(mS). This and the fact that n is finitely generated implies that n^t \subset mS for some t >= 1'

proof.text: Proof of (1). For every $k\ge1$, $(\mathfrak mS)^k=\mathfrak m^kS$ (both are generated by the products $\varphi(a_1)\cdots\varphi(a_k)$, $a_i\in\mathfrak m$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-change-ideal-completion] to the ring $A=S$, the module $M=S$, $I=\mathfrak n$, $J=\mathfrak mS$, $c=t$ (Step 2) and $d=1$ ($\mathfrak mS\subseteq\mathfrak n$): the map $\theta:\varprojlim_kS/(\mathfrak mS)^k=S'\to\varprojlim_kS/\mathfrak n^k=S^\wedge$, $(x_k)_k\mapsto(x_k\bmod\mathfrak n^k)_k$, is a ring isomorphism. This $\theta$ is the map $\gamma$ of the statement, so $\gamma$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Construct the canonical ring map ψ from the completed source to the completion for mS by AdicCompletion.liftRingHom applied to quotientMap composed with evalₐ. Compatibility follows from the inverse-limit property, and evalₐ_liftRingHom gives the coordinate formula. Compose with γ to get φhat and its required coordinate formula.

The coordinate formula determines the restriction of ψ along R to be the original φ action. This yields the scalar tower. IsHausdorff.map_algebraMap_iff first restricts Hausdorffness of the mS-adic completion to m and then extends it to mR-completion. The completed base is complete for mR-completion by AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete_self. The finite reduction hypothesis needed by 031D is supplied by the new reduction lemma.

Apply Module.finite_and_span_eq_top_of_adicComplete to S completed along mS over R-completion. Its first conjunct gives ψ.Finite. The ring equivalence γ is finite by surjectivity, and RingHom.Finite.comp transports finiteness to φhat = γ ∘ ψ.

lean.statement: theorem finite_after_completion (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] (m : Ideal R) (n : Ideal S) (φ : R →+* S) (hm : m = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (hn : n = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) [IsLocalHom φ] (hm_fg : m.FG) (hn_fg : n.FG) (hfinite : letI := (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.map φ m) φ Ideal.le_comap_map).toAlgebra Module.Finite (R ⧸ m) (S ⧸ Ideal.map φ m)) : ∃ (γ : AdicCompletion (Ideal.map φ m) S ≃+* AdicCompletion n S) (φhat : AdicCompletion m R →+* AdicCompletion n S), (∀ (k : ℕ) (x : AdicCompletion (Ideal.map φ m) S) (s : S), AdicCompletion.evalₐ (Ideal.map φ m) k x = Ideal.Quotient.mk ((Ideal.map φ m) ^ k) s → AdicCompletion.evalₐ n k (γ x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (n ^ k) s) ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ) (x : AdicCompletion m R) (r : R), AdicCompletion.evalₐ m k x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (m ^ k) r → AdicCompletion.evalₐ n k (φhat x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (n ^ k) (φ r)) ∧ letI := φhat.toAlgebra Module.Finite (AdicCompletion m R) (AdicCompletion n S)
